text: Davyd Whaley (December 6, 1967 – October 15, 2014) was an American abstract painter recognized for incorporating Jungian themes related to the subconscious in his artwork. Born in Bristol, Tennessee, in 1967, Whaley lived and worked in Los Angeles. He served as a United States Navy veteran for four years and had a twenty-year career as an electrical engineer before transitioning to painting. In 2004, he met television director Norman Buckley, with whom he married as soon as legally permitted in 2008, remaining married until Whaley's death on October 15, 2014, in Los Angeles. Whaley was primarily self-taught but studied painting at the Art Students League of New York from 2008 to 2011, working under mentors Ronnie Landfield and Larry Poons. His style is characterized by brilliant colors and a focus on Jungian themes, reflecting his interest in dream analysis and the subconscious. His paintings appeared on various television shows, including CSI: Crime Scene Investigation, Californication, and Pretty Little Liars. He relocated his studio from his home to the Santa Fe Art Colony in downtown Los Angeles. In 2016, the Davyd Whaley Foundation was established by his husband, Norman Buckley, to honor Whaley's legacy of service by awarding grants to artists. Whaley was a philanthropist who taught art to underprivileged individuals, counseled grieving families in hospitals, and taught terminally-ill and war-scarred children to paint. He was honored as Volunteer of the Year by the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors in 2012. His core goals—making art, purchasing art by others, helping people whenever possible, and growing in consciousness—formed the foundation's mission. A monograph of his work was published in 2016, featuring an essay titled "A Hero's Journey" by Peter Clothier.
